en: The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika), The Two Triplets of the Internal (Ajjhattattikadvaya)
A wholesome internal state is related to an internal unwholesome state by way of object-condition.

(Abbreviated. There are eighteen [relations] in the case of the object, nine in the case of the dominant, eighteen in the case of the decisive support, six in the case of the prenascence, three in the case of the nutriment, and six each in the cases of presence and non-disappearance.
A wholesome external state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state that is neither internal nor external.
(Abbreviated. [In the object-condition there are] eighteen; in the predominance-condition, fifteen; in the decisive-support-condition, eighteen;
in the prenascence-condition, six; in the nutriment-condition, three; in the presence and non-disappearance conditions, six.
Dependent on a wholesome state with an internal object, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor has an internal object by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. There are nine under root; nine under predominance … pe … three under mutuality … pe … three under resultant … pe … nine under non-disappearance.
Dependent on a wholesome state with an external object, there arises an unwholesome state that does not have an external object, by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. There are nine [conditions] for root; nine for predominance … pe … three for mutuality … pe … three for result … pe … nine for non-disappearance.
